risk: Fictitious vendors are created, or bank details on genuine vendors are altered, so payments leave the organisation to accounts controlled by a fraudster.
audit_objective: Confirm vendor records are created and amended only on verified, authorised information.
what_to_review: Authorisation and independent verification of vendor creation and bank changes
Call-back verification to independently obtained contact details
Duplicate vendor detection
Employee-to-vendor data matching
Dormant vendor reactivation and one-time vendor use
procedures: Extract the vendor master change log and test creations and bank changes for independent verification evidence.
Match the vendor master against employee data on bank account, address, tax identifier and phone.
Run duplicate analytics across name, bank account and tax identifier; quantify spend flowing through duplicates.
Identify vendors reactivated after dormancy and test the first payment following reactivation.
Test one-time and manual vendor payments for approval and business justification.
red_flags: Bank change immediately followed by a large payment
Vendors sharing a bank account with each other or an employee
Vendor created and paid within the same day
Verification evidenced by an email from the address that requested the change
evidence: Vendor master change log with user and timestamp
plain: Set up a fake supplier, or change a real one's bank details, and payments walk straight out of the company.

risk: Suppliers are awarded work without competition or on terms that favour them, often where a personal interest exists.
audit_objective: Assess whether sourcing is competitive, documented and free from undisclosed interest.
what_to_review: Tender thresholds and adherence to them
Evaluation criteria, scoring and evaluator independence
Single and sole-source justifications
Conflict of interest declarations from evaluators
Contract award terms versus what was tendered
procedures: Quantify spend awarded without competition and test the justification for the largest.
Re-perform the scoring on a sample of tenders and test whether the award followed the evaluation.
Test evaluator conflict declarations and match evaluators to winning suppliers for connections.
Compare final contract terms to the tendered terms and identify post-award concessions.
Test for purchases split to fall below the tender threshold.
red_flags: Sole-source justification citing urgency repeatedly
Scoring changed after bids were opened
The same supplier winning every category with one buyer
Contracts amended in the supplier's favour shortly after award
evidence: Spend analysis by supplier and buyer
plain: Awarding work without competition costs money, and is often where undisclosed personal interests hide.

risk: Commitments are made without budget or authority, so the organisation is bound to spend that was never approved.
audit_objective: Confirm purchase commitments are authorised within delegated authority and budget before they are made.
what_to_review: Delegated authority matrix and its configuration in the system
Budget availability checking at requisition
Retrospective purchase orders raised after the invoice arrives
Order splitting below approval thresholds
Blanket and standing orders and their monitoring
procedures: Test the system configuration of approval limits against the delegated authority matrix.
Quantify purchase orders raised on or after the invoice date and test the reason for each.
Analyse orders clustering just below authority thresholds by requisitioner.
Test blanket order utilisation against approved values and expiry.
Test a sample of orders for budget availability checking at the time of commitment.
red_flags: A high proportion of retrospective orders in one department
Values repeatedly just under a threshold
Approvers approving their own requisitions through delegation
Blanket orders extended year after year without re-approval
evidence: Purchase order data with approval trail
plain: An approved order is the point at which the company becomes committed to spend. After that it is too late.

risk: Goods or services are recorded as received when they were not, allowing payment for nothing — the hardest step to verify for services.
audit_objective: Confirm receipt is independently evidenced before payment, including for services and intangibles.
what_to_review: Segregation between ordering, receiving and payment approval
Evidence required to confirm receipt of services and consultancy
Receipts entered by the requisitioner
Quantity and quality verification against the order
Goods received not invoiced ageing
procedures: Test whether the person confirming receipt is independent of the person who ordered, and quantify exceptions.
For service purchases, test the evidence supporting confirmation — deliverables, timesheets, reports — rather than an approval click.
Reconcile goods received to purchase orders and to invoices; investigate receipts with no order.
Age the goods received not invoiced balance and test the oldest items for validity.
red_flags: Receipt confirmed on the same day the invoice was entered
Consultancy accepted with no deliverable on file
One person ordering and receiving in a remote location
GRNI balances aged over a year and never cleared
plain: Confirming that goods or services arrived is what stops the company paying for nothing, and it is hardest to prove for services.

risk: Invoices are paid without matching to an order and a receipt, so overbilling and unordered supply are paid in full.
audit_objective: Confirm invoices are matched to order and receipt, and that exceptions are resolved rather than overridden.
what_to_review: Three-way match configuration and tolerance settings
Volume and pattern of match exceptions and overrides
Invoices paid without a purchase order and their approval route
Coding accuracy and approval of expense allocation
Optical character recognition and automated posting controls
procedures: Quantify invoices paid without a matched order or receipt and test the approval for a sample.
Analyse match tolerance overrides by user and value; test whether tolerances are set at a level that makes the match meaningful.
Re-perform the match on a sample of paid invoices and quantify variances.
Test invoices coded to unusual or generic accounts for validity.
red_flags: Tolerances so wide that almost nothing fails the match
Overrides concentrated with a small number of users
Non-PO invoices used routinely by a department
Invoices approved by the person who requested and received
plain: Matching the invoice to the order and the delivery is the basic check that stops overbilling.

risk: The payment file is altered after approval, or payments are released outside the normal run, moving funds without the approvals the process assumes.
audit_objective: Confirm that only approved invoices are paid, in the approved amount, to the approved account.
what_to_review: Payment run preparation, review and dual release at the bank
Integrity of the file between the ledger and the bank
Manual, urgent and emergency payments
Bank mandates and signatory currency
Positive pay or equivalent bank-side controls
procedures: Agree the total and record count of an approved payment proposal to the file transmitted to the bank.
Test that bank release requires two approvers independent of invoice processing, including for urgent payments.
Extract all manual and emergency payments and test authorisation and justification for each.
Confirm mandates and signatories against the approved list and identify leavers still authorised.
red_flags: Urgent payments used routinely rather than exceptionally
File totals differing from the approved proposal
Payments to vendors added on the day of the run
Signatories who left months ago still active
plain: This is the moment cash actually leaves. Everything before it is preparation.

risk: The same invoice is paid twice, or paid to the wrong vendor, and the loss is never identified because no one looks.
audit_objective: Determine whether duplicate and erroneous payments occur and whether they are detected and recovered.
what_to_review: Duplicate detection controls at invoice entry and at payment
Invoice numbering conventions that defeat detection
Recovery process for identified duplicates
Credit balances on vendor accounts
Statement reconciliation with major vendors
procedures: Run duplicate analytics on exact and fuzzy matches across vendor, amount, invoice number and date; quantify the exposure.
Test whether identified duplicates were recovered and how long recovery took.
Review vendor accounts with debit balances or long-standing credits, which often indicate unrecovered duplicates.
Test whether vendor statement reconciliations are performed for the largest suppliers.
red_flags: Duplicate detection limited to exact invoice number matches
Vendor credit balances aged over a year
Recoveries pursued only when the vendor volunteers them
Same invoice entered against two vendor records
plain: Paying the same invoice twice is common, rarely noticed, and usually only recovered if someone looks.

risk: Personal expenditure is claimed as business expense, or purchase cards are used outside policy, with approval given without scrutiny.
audit_objective: Assess whether expense and card spend is within policy, supported and genuinely reviewed.
what_to_review: Expense policy limits, receipt requirements and approval routing
Purchase card issuance, limits and merchant category restrictions
Approval quality — whether approvers examine or simply click
Cash withdrawals, round-sum and weekend transactions
Card cancellation on exit and dormant card review
procedures: Analyse claims by claimant for round sums, duplicated receipts, weekend and holiday spend, and amounts just under the receipt threshold.
Test purchase card transactions against merchant category restrictions and policy.
Measure approval time per claim; approvals granted seconds apart indicate no review.
Test that cards were cancelled for leavers and review dormant cards still active.
Test a sample of claims to original receipts rather than a summary.
red_flags: Claims consistently just below the receipt threshold
Approvals batched in seconds
Cards active for staff who left
Cash withdrawals on purchase cards
plain: Expenses and company cards are small amounts approved quickly, which is exactly why personal spending slips through.

risk: The organisation pays more than the contract allows because no one checks invoices against negotiated rates, rebates and service credits.
audit_objective: Confirm that the value negotiated in contracts is actually realised in what is paid.
what_to_review: Contracted rates loaded into the system versus applied at invoicing
Indexation and price increase clauses and their application
Volume rebates and discounts earned and claimed
Service credits for failure and whether they are taken
Contract expiry, renewal and evergreen terms
procedures: Re-price a sample of invoices against the contract and quantify overcharges across the supplier base.
Recompute contractual indexation applied and test that increases were permitted and correctly calculated.
Recompute rebates earned against volumes and test whether they were claimed and received.
Test service level performance against the contract and whether credits due were deducted.
red_flags: Price increases applied earlier or larger than the contract permits
Rebates never claimed
Service failures with no credits taken
Contracts auto-renewing at uncompetitive rates
plain: Companies negotiate good rates and then pay something different, because nobody checks the invoice against the contract.

subprocess: Procurement Fraud, Kickbacks and Conflicts of Interest
risk: Buyers receive undisclosed benefit for directing business, inflating prices and distorting supplier selection.
audit_objective: Detect indicators of collusion between buyers and suppliers and assess the controls that would prevent it.
what_to_review: Conflict of interest declarations from procurement and budget holders
Gifts and hospitality register and its completeness
Supplier concentration by buyer and price trends
Bid patterns suggesting collusion among suppliers
Rotation of buyer responsibilities and mandatory leave
procedures: Analyse spend by buyer and supplier to identify concentrations, then compare prices paid against market or other business units.
Match supplier data against employee data — addresses, phone numbers, bank accounts and company registry directorships.
Review bid patterns for consistent losing bidders, near-identical pricing, or rotating winners.
Reconcile the gifts and hospitality register to expenses claimed by suppliers where visible, and test declaration completeness.
Test whether buyer rotation and leave requirements were applied.
red_flags: A buyer whose suppliers price consistently above market
Losing bidders that never win but always bid
Gifts register with almost no entries in a large function
Suppliers registered at a residential address
evidence: Spend analysis by buyer and supplier
plain: Buyers control who gets the business, which makes them a target for suppliers offering something on the side.

subprocess: Accruals, Cut-Off and Accounts Payable Integrity
risk: Liabilities are omitted at period end, or the payables ledger contains balances that no longer represent real obligations.
audit_objective: Confirm that payables and accruals are complete, valid and correctly cut off.
what_to_review: Completeness of accruals for goods and services received not invoiced
Cut-off testing around period end
Ageing of the payables ledger and old unpaid balances
Debit balances and unapplied credits in payables
Reconciliation of payables ledger to the general ledger
procedures: Test cut-off by examining invoices received after period end and tracing them to the correct period.
Test the accrual calculation against the goods received not invoiced report and known service commitments.
Age the payables ledger and investigate balances outstanding beyond normal terms — they may be disputed, duplicated or fictitious.
Reconcile the subledger to the general ledger and test reconciling items.
red_flags: Accruals estimated as a flat percentage with no underlying data
Old payables balances never queried by the supplier
Reconciling items rolling forward every period
Invoices held in a drawer until the new period
plain: Leaving out bills that have already been incurred makes profit look better than it is.
